differentiation.occupancy_preservation: Minimizing negative Jensen-Shannon divergence rewards distinguishable source and target assignment distributions; minimizing the overlap penalty directly discourages both endpoints from using the same codes. The source-marginal entropy term discourages concentrated source usage. All three components update codewords through the soft assignments; none minimizes the distance between the two endpoint codewords.

vs_r8.why: Unlike inert encoder-only terms, this objective directly differentiates through the codebook. Unlike pairwise convergence mechanisms, it rewards assignment-distribution separation and penalizes endpoint assignment overlap rather than asking one code to serve both endpoints. Its explicit source entropy term also targets code concentration, rather than accepting concentration as the route to higher pair-level ER.

differentiation.vs_reference_arm: the reference arm is the untouched host; this candidate adds one term whose gradient reaches the codebook without pulling a transition's two codewords together

equation: For each valid pair define p_s(c)=softmax_c(-||source-codebook_c||^2/tau) and p_t(c)=softmax_c(-||target-codebook_c||^2/tau). Let m=(p_s+p_t)/2 and J=0.5*KL(p_s||m)+0.5*KL(p_t||m). Let H(u)=-sum_c u_c log(u_c+epsilon), where u is the masked mean of p_s over source endpoints. L=weight*(-J + balance_weight*(H(u)-log(C)) + repel_weight*mean_b sum_c p_s(c)*p_t(c)).
expected_failure_modes: Assignment separation can encode transition-specific distinctions that are too fine-grained or unstable for held-out transitions. The entropy term balances only the source marginal, so target usage, prefix branching, or train-to-test frequency drift may still worsen; soft separation may also fail to change hard assignments.

forbidden_substitutions.reason: a quota on the assignment is the family that produced 39.5% and 24.2% occupancy without preserving the exported codes
a term that pulls a pair's two codewords together is what collapsed the level-0 codebook to two codes

hypotheses: Reject if exported level-0 Gini exceeds 0.216, L1-to-L2 branches fall below 65.91 per L1 code, train-to-test frequency drift grows, sequence information falls, or the single held-out Stage-3 recall@10 does not exceed 0.06406796775709883.

symbols.H(u): Entropy of the mean source assignment distribution.
symbols.J: Jensen-Shannon divergence between the directed endpoint assignment distributions.
symbols.KL(a||b): Kullback-Leibler divergence from distribution a to distribution b.
symbols.balance_weight: Coefficient on the source assignment entropy term.
symbols.epsilon: Positive constant for numerical stability in the logarithm.
symbols.m: Mean of the source and target assignment distributions for a pair.
symbols.p_s(c): Soft source assignment probability for codeword c.
symbols.p_t(c): Soft target assignment probability for codeword c.
symbols.repel_weight: Coefficient on the endpoint assignment overlap penalty.
symbols.u: Masked mean source assignment distribution across the batch.
symbols.weight: Overall coefficient multiplying this auxiliary loss.

tests.statement: the term's value on a hand-computable case matches the declared equation
the gradient reaches exactly the declared parameter groups
